title_en: Chinese TV Dramas (3/20): Showdown at the Evidence Board
note_en: 善于 (shànyú, "be good at") is followed directly by a verb phrase: 善于从细节中发现……线索 "good at finding clues in the details." English needs "at" plus an -ing form; Chinese simply lines the verbs up, so 善于发现 is literally "good-at find." The same pattern works with similar verbs such as 擅长 and 喜欢.

sentences.en: Crime dramas have a long history on Chinese television. From Serious Crimes Unit 6, which began airing in the early 2000s, to the later Day and Night, they have produced landmark shows that left a deep impression on audiences: the former is known for its realistic portrayal of police work, while the latter won wide acclaim for its intense suspense.

sentences.en: The two most representative titles in the Mist Theater lineup are The Bad Kids and The Long Night. The first tells how a few children who witness an accidental death are drawn step by step into lies and crime; the second is the story of a prosecutor who pays a huge price to clear the name of a man who was wrongly convicted.

sentences.en: Crime dramas often pair a seasoned veteran cop with a rookie: the veteran relies on instinct and experience to spot clues quickly, while the rookie runs errands and digs through records, and as they learn to work together they gradually build trust and an unspoken understanding. Meanwhile, the medical examiner's autopsy report is often the key piece of evidence that sets up a plot twist.

sentences.en: Many crime dramas are inspired by real cases, but to protect privacy and avoid misleading viewers, writers usually change the times, places, and names, and put a disclaimer at the start saying "This story is entirely fictional." And because censors keep a tight rein on violent and bloody images, crime scenes are usually shown with considerable restraint.

sentences.en: An important branch of the crime drama is the undercover drama, in which the hero has to assume a false identity and spend a long time inside a criminal gang gathering evidence, under enormous psychological pressure from the constant risk of being exposed. In addition, shows such as anti-drug dramas and anti-gang dramas, which stress that justice will prevail and promote "positive energy" (zheng nengliang, officially encouraged uplifting content), generally find it easier to win official support and promotional resources.

sentences.en: In recent years, the most acclaimed crime dramas have paid more and more attention to storytelling technique, often using multiple storylines or flashbacks so that the truth about a case is pieced together gradually from different characters' memories. Viewers in the danmu (bullet comments that scroll across the screen) also love guessing who the real killer is as they watch, and anyone who guesses right earns likes and recognition from other viewers.

sentences.en: The success of Mist Theater also prompted other platforms to launch similar suspense-drama brands one after another, trying to copy its business model of releasing a concentrated run of high-quality short series to hold on to a core audience. In the end, the reason crime dramas have kept a steady audience for so long is that they satisfy people's hope that justice will eventually triumph over evil, while also making them face the complex, and even dark, side of human nature.
